questions.prompt: A colleague says the laptop has internet but their work website does not load. What steps do you take?
questions.objective: Isolate scope and use evidence before changing settings.
rubric: Clarifies one website versus all websites
Checks DNS, browser, network and service status in order
Records the result and escalates without unnecessary risky changes
questions.sample_structure: Clarify impact → reproduce safely → isolate device/network/service → try minimal reversible steps → communicate next action.
questions.source: Original OverseasJob.in editorial exercise; not an employer assessment

questions.prompt: How would you handle a suspicious email reported by a colleague?
questions.objective: Explain safe incident handling and communication.
rubric: Does not click suspect links or download attachments
Guides colleague without blame and limits further exposure
questions.sample_structure: Contain → report using approved channel → collect safe metadata → advise user → follow up.
questions.source: Original OverseasJob.in editorial exercise; not an employer assessment

questions.prompt: Two support tickets arrive: one printer failure and one company-wide sign-in outage. How do you prioritise?
rubric: Documents prioritisation and follows escalation policy
questions.sample_structure: Assess severity → respond to widespread outage → update ticket owners → return to lower-impact ticket.
questions.source: Original OverseasJob.in editorial exercise; not an employer assessment

questions.prompt: Describe a time you had to learn an unfamiliar tool to solve an issue.
questions.objective: Use truthful structured example and reflection.
rubric: Describes result or lessons without exaggerating
questions.sample_structure: Situation → task → action → actual result or learning.

questions.prompt: A customer says the issue has been reported three times and is still unresolved. What would you say?
questions.objective: Show ownership, empathy and concrete follow-through.
rubric: Explains next step and follow-up time
questions.sample_structure: Acknowledge frustration → summarise issue → check case history → offer realistic escalation/follow-up.

questions.prompt: You do not know the answer to a customer’s product question. What do you do?
rubric: Communicates when and how a verified response will be provided

questions.prompt: A customer asks for a refund outside the published policy. How would you respond?

questions.prompt: Tell us about a time you de-escalated a tense conversation.

questions.prompt: How do you protect private information in a shared office spreadsheet?
